subject.title: [Bug]: Clarify Telegram channel_post auth when groups[chatId].allowFrom is configured

question: For Telegram channel_post native commands, should a configured groups[chatId].allowFrom sender allowlist be ignored in favor of explicit chat allow, or should channel_post fail closed as unsupported when sender-scoped auth is configured?
rationale: Telegram channel_post may not provide a human sender, while OpenClaw models groups[chatId].allowFrom as sender-scoped authorization; automation should not choose that security boundary without maintainer intent.

options.title: Fail Closed On Sender Allowlist
options.body: Treat channel_post commands as unsupported when per-chat sender allowFrom is configured, return a clear denial or diagnostic, and document that no human sender is available.

options.title: Use Explicit Chat Allow Only
options.body: Permit channel_post commands from explicitly configured channel chats and document that sender-scoped allowFrom is intentionally ignored for channel posts.

options.title: Defer To Bot-To-Bot Policy
options.body: Keep this issue open until broader Telegram bot-to-bot policy work settles channel identity, peer-bot, and loop-control semantics together.

recommendation.title: Fail Closed On Sender Allowlist
recommendation.body: Treat channel_post commands as unsupported when per-chat sender allowFrom is configured, return a clear denial or diagnostic, and document that no human sender is available.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest inspected history on Telegram access policy/docs and is the best available owner for deciding this security boundary.
